plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Rows of cup-shaped blooms stretch across the bulb fields and gardens of the Netherlands. They make ribbons of scarlet, canary yellow, magenta and snowy white. Mid-April is when the display looks its most painterly.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early April to early May, with peak bloom in mid-to-late April
plants.location: Keukenhof and the bulb-growing region of the Netherlands
plants.funFact: Tulips came to Europe from Central Asia by way of the Ottoman Empire. In the 1600s Dutch 'tulip mania' drove single bulbs to prices that rivaled grand townhouses.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Dense spikes of deep blue, white-tipped flowers spill across Texas roadsides and meadows. In peak years they look like a rolling blue sea. In mid-April the display moves north into the prairies of North Texas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly March to April, starting in South Texas and peaking in mid-April farther north
plants.location: Texas, USA, from the Hill Country to the northern prairies
plants.funFact: The Texas bluebonnet is the state flower of Texas. The white tip on each blossom turns magenta as the flower ages, which signals to pollinators that it is past its nectar prime.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Cosmos has daisy-like flowers on feathery, fern-fine foliage. In autumn it floods the roadsides and veld of South Africa's Highveld with pink, magenta and white. The blooms nod in the breeze for a few short weeks.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April (southern autumn) in the Highveld
plants.location: Highveld of Gauteng and the Free State, South Africa
plants.funFact: Cosmos is native to Mexico, but it has naturalized so widely in South Africa that its autumn bloom has become a seasonal landmark. Its name comes from a Greek word for 'order' or 'harmony,' a nod to its evenly arranged petals.
